title: Improving developer velocity with AI-ready architecture
challenge: A growing Next.js application had blurred domain boundaries and inconsistent conventions, slowing onboarding and causing AI coding tools to apply outdated patterns.
approach: Created localized documentation across application domains, established repository-wide Copilot guidance, and configured a Playwright MCP workflow so AI agents could inspect and validate browser behavior in local development.
accessibility: Built WCAG 2.1 AA expectations and performance budgets into the shared engineering guidance so generated implementations favor semantic HTML and lean client components.
outcome: Made project conventions easier for new contributors and AI-assisted workflows to discover, reducing review churn and improving first-pass test alignment.

title: Simplifying loan-offer selection across devices
challenge: A multi-step partner-funnel flow created cognitive friction, and offer states could be ambiguous when no option was preselected or rates varied.
approach: Delivered a responsive single-screen offer experience with featured and selectable cards, fallback logic for unselected offers, and viewport-aware ordering for desktop and mobile layouts.
accessibility: Implemented keyboard-operable selection with explicit selected and checked states. CSS Grid transitions limited layout shift while memoized sorting avoided unnecessary rerenders.
outcome: Removed empty-state failures and created a faster, clearer offer-selection interaction for a high-traffic financial-services funnel.

title: Raising the accessibility baseline across a web application
challenge: Accessibility audits identified missing bypass navigation, incomplete asynchronous validation announcements, inconsistent focus behavior, and motion triggers across shared experiences.
approach: Introduced a global skip link, semantic form-error associations and live regions, standardized keyboard support and visible focus states, and added reduced-motion safeguards.
accessibility: Validated patterns against WCAG 2.1 AA expectations and screen-reader behavior while preserving approved visual design and existing analytics.
outcome: Resolved compliance risks across primary customer journeys and translated accessibility requirements into repeatable PR criteria and automated test coverage.

title: Making regulatory disclosures self-service and secure
challenge: Legal and marketing teams needed to update disclosures quickly without raw CMS HTML, inconsistent design, or avoidable security and accessibility risk.
approach: Connected CMS rich-text links to version-controlled dialog components, allowing editors to select approved disclosures while the application safely rendered the matching modal.
accessibility: Implemented labeled dialogs with focus trapping, Escape-key support, and focus return. Dialog content was loaded on interaction to keep initial payloads lean.
outcome: Enabled stakeholders to place approved disclosures independently while preserving consistent presentation, accessible interactions, and controlled content delivery.
